_readme: Level 3 worksheet hints (Level3WorksheetHints, T06). HINT on Bea's worksheet opens only after the first complete check, for a place that check marked with ?.

Each set lists the decision ids it helps with (Level3WorksheetCheck.DecisionIds) and exactly three hints: 1 where to look (a record, Bea, or a Tax Code Book section), 2 the idea, 3 specific help. Every decision must have one set.

Teaching pass (6 November 2026): each brief opens with the matching Section 4 question (earned? for the business? supported? already counted?) and points to where to look; it never names a category or reason. Revised T06 (paper machine): a set may add one optional brief line for the compact batch/note cards after a Check batch marks a decision with ?. It points to where to look, never the answer; the idea (line 2) follows a repeated look-again. Line 3 is never shown by the machine.
Hints are free: they never change the grade, XP, coins or Public Trust, and are not saved. They must not appear before a check, and the book leaves (book.json) never state Bea's answers.
A broken file is reported in the Console and the built-in copy (Level3WorksheetHints.BuiltIn) is used.
Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored by the game.

hints.brief: Was it earned? Read who paid Bea, and for what work.
lines: Read Bea's Studio fees sheet: who paid her, and for what work?
Money Bea earned from her design work is what her costs are taken from.
Studio fees go in Income.

hints.brief: For the business, and supported? Read its record. Book, Section 4.
lines: Read the cost schedule row and the record that backs it. Tax Code Book, Section 4: Costs and Purpose.
This was paid for the studio's work, in 2026, and a record shows it.
A supported business cost of the year goes in Allowable expenses.

hints.brief: Was it for the business? Read the receipt, or ask Bea.
lines: Read the Party shop receipt again, or ask Bea: what was it for? Tax Code Book, Section 4.
A cost lowers Bea's income only if it was spent to earn her fees. Her own celebration wasn't.
Put the party purchases in Not deductible.

hints.brief: Already counted? Compare the Print bill with the Cost schedule.
lines: Compare the Print bill with the Cost schedule. Tax Code Book, Section 5: Count Once.
Both papers show the same printing order, PRINT-26. Counting the bill as well would count it twice.
Keep the printing bill in Supporting only: it backs up the schedule's row.

hints.brief: Which question does it fail? Think about what it was for.
lines: Ask Bea what the party purchases were for.
Was the dinner for the studio's work, or for her own celebration?
Choose Personal purpose.

hints.brief: Which question does it fail? Look for PRINT-26 on her papers.
lines: Look for PRINT-26 on Bea's other papers. Tax Code Book, Section 5: Count Once.
Bea's draft adds the printing bill on top of a cost schedule that already includes it.
Choose Already represented.
Which worksheet row already records the same printing order?
Look for the row with the same reference, PRINT-26, on the Cost schedule.
Link it to Printing and supplies, the Cost schedule's row.
A subtotal adds exactly the strips in its own section, each once.
Tap the SUBTOTAL slot, then each strip in the section with + between them, then =, and attach the tape.
Check no strip is missing, typed by hand, counted twice or taken from another section.
